question: According to the manual, why might steering be a better choice than braking when a driver suddenly faces an obstacle in the road?
choice_a: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Steering causes less tire wear than braking
choice_c: State law requires drivers to steer before braking
choice_d: Steering keeps the engine running more smoothly
explanation: The manual states you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, though it warns top-heavy vehicles and multiple trailers may flip over.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: What does the manual recommend as the best way to be ready to make a firm, quick emergency turn?
choice_a: Rest one hand on the door while driving
choice_b: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times
choice_c: Keep one hand near the parking brake
choice_d: Grip the wheel only when traffic is heavy
explanation: The manual says the best way to have both hands on the wheel in an emergency is to keep them there all the time.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: Why should a driver avoid applying the brake while making a quick emergency steering maneuver?
choice_a: It voids the vehicle's warranty
choice_b: It slows the turn down too much to be useful
choice_c: It can easily lock the wheels and cause a skid
choice_d: It triggers the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: The manual warns it's very easy to lock your wheels while turning and braking, which can cause a skid out of control.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: What risk does the manual associate with turning the steering wheel more sharply than needed to clear an obstacle?
choice_a: Faster tire wear only
choice_b: Reduced fuel economy
choice_c: A citation for an illegal lane change
choice_d: A greater chance of a skid or rollover
explanation: The manual states the more sharply you turn, the greater the chances of a skid or rollover.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: If an oncoming vehicle has drifted into your lane, which direction does the manual say is generally best to steer?
choice_a: To your right
choice_b: To your left, toward the oncoming lane
choice_c: Straight ahead while braking hard
choice_d: Whichever direction has heavier traffic
explanation: The manual says if an oncoming driver has drifted into your lane, a move to your right is best, since the natural response is for the other driver to return to their own lane.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: If you are blocked on both sides and must steer to avoid a collision, why does the manual recommend moving to the right?
choice_a: The right shoulder is closer to your destination
choice_b: It avoids forcing anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision
choice_c: Right turns require less steering wheel movement
choice_d: The right shoulder is always paved
explanation: The manual states that if blocked on both sides, moving right is best because you won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: If forced to drive off the road in an emergency, what does the manual say about braking?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible immediately
choice_b: Never brake once you have left the pavement
choice_c: Avoid braking, if possible, until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently
choice_d: Only use the parking brake once off the road
explanation: The manual advises avoiding braking until speed drops to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: When returning to the road after driving onto the shoulder, why does the manual warn against edging back onto the pavement gradually?
choice_a: It takes too much time in an emergency
choice_b: It can trigger the ABS system unnecessarily
choice_c: It is against traffic law in every state
choice_d: Your tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control
explanation: The manual warns not to edge gradually back onto the road because the tires might grab unexpectedly, causing loss of control; instead, turn sharply enough to get back on safely.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: When using the stab braking method, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after the brakes are released?
choice_a: Up to one second
choice_b: Up to five seconds
choice_c: Up to ten seconds
choice_d: Wheels start rolling instantly
explanation: The manual notes it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after you release the brakes during stab braking.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.17 — Driving Emergencies

question: How does an Antilock Braking System (ABS) function, according to the manual?
choice_a: It increases brake pressure whenever the vehicle is turning
choice_b: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup and an electronic control unit decreases brake pressure to avoid it
choice_c: It disables the brakes above a certain speed
choice_d: It replaces the vehicle's normal brakes entirely
explanation: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and the electronic control unit (ECU) decreases brake pressure to avoid it, working far faster than a driver can respond.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Per the manual, ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after which date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1999
choice_c: March 1, 1997
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: The manual states ABS is required on hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or more if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: January 1, 1999
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Where will a trailer's yellow ABS malfunction lamp be located, according to the manual?
choice_a: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_b: On the right side only
choice_c: On the rear bumper only
choice_d: Inside the cab dashboard
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: On older ABS systems, until what speed might the malfunction lamp stay on after the startup bulb check?
choice_a: 15 mph
choice_b: Five mph
choice_c: 25 mph
choice_d: 35 mph
explanation: The manual notes that on older systems, the malfunction lamp could stay on until you are driving over five mph.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: When only the tractor has ABS (and the trailer does not), what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Never brake at all in that combination
choice_b: Disconnect the trailer immediately
choice_c: You should maintain steering control with less chance of jackknifing, but watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it swings out
choice_d: Apply the parking brake instead of the service brake
explanation: The manual states that with ABS only on the tractor, you should be able to maintain steering control with less chance of jackknifing, but should watch the trailer and let up on the brakes if it begins to swing out.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What is the one exception to the normal ABS braking procedure described in the manual?
choice_a: You may disable ABS during rain
choice_b: You should always brake gently regardless of ABS
choice_c: ABS should never be fully applied under any circumstance
choice_d: If your vehicle has working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop
explanation: The manual's only exception is that if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual's ABS safety reminders, what remains the best vehicle safety feature?
choice_a: A safe driver
choice_b: The antilock braking system itself
choice_c: Dual rear tires
choice_d: The parking brake
explanation: The manual reminds drivers that the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver, and that ABS is only an add-on to normal brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.18 — Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four causes of skids listed in the manual?
choice_a: Over-braking
choice_b: Underinflated tires
choice_c: Over-steering
choice_d: Driving too fast for conditions
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast as the four causes of skids; underinflated tires is not among them.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: What does the manual identify as the most common type of skid?
choice_a: A front-wheel skid caused by worn tires
choice_b: A skid caused by crosswinds
choice_c: A drive-wheel skid in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
choice_d: A skid caused by defective steering linkage
explanation: The manual states by far the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: What is the first step the manual gives for correcting a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Turn the wheel sharply toward the shoulder
choice_b: Apply the parking brake
choice_c: Accelerate to regain traction
choice_d: Stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again
explanation: The manual says to stop braking first, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding further.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: Why must a driver countersteer after turning back on course during skid recovery?
choice_a: Because the vehicle has a tendency to keep on turning, and without countersteering you may skid the opposite direction
choice_b: Because the steering wheel automatically locks
choice_c: Because state law requires it
choice_d: Because it improves fuel economy
explanation: The manual explains that as a vehicle turns back on course it tends to keep turning, so you must countersteer quickly or risk skidding in the opposite direction.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: Besides driving too fast for conditions, what else does the manual list as a cause of front-wheel skids?
choice_a: Overinflated rear tires
choice_b: Lack of tread on the front tires or cargo loaded so not enough weight is on the front axle
choice_c: A malfunctioning ABS lamp
choice_d: Using the engine brake on dry pavement
explanation: The manual lists lack of tread on the front tires and cargo loaded so not enough weight is on the front axle as additional causes of front-wheel skids.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what is the only way to stop a front-wheel skid once it begins?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel harder into the skid
choice_b: Apply the brakes firmly
choice_c: Let the vehicle slow down as quickly as possible without skidding
choice_d: Shift into a higher gear
explanation: The manual states that when a front-wheel skid occurs, the only way to stop it is to let the vehicle slow down, stopping turning and/or braking so hard.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.19 — Skid Control and Recovery

question: What are the three basic steps the manual says to take at any crash?
choice_a: Call your dispatcher, take photos, and exchange insurance
choice_b: Move all vehicles immediately, call a tow truck, and leave
choice_c: Assess damage, file a report, and wait for police
choice_d: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
explanation: The manual lists the basic steps at any crash as protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.20 — Crash Procedures

question: What should you do to protect a crash area, per the manual?
choice_a: Put on your flashers and set out reflective triangles to warn other traffic
choice_b: Turn off all vehicle lights so as not to distract other drivers
choice_c: Wait for police before setting out reflective triangles
choice_d: Leave the scene to avoid liability
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to put on their flashers and set out reflective triangles to warn other traffic in time to avoid the crash.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.20 — Crash Procedures

question: If you have a cell phone or CB radio after a crash, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Wait until the scene is cleared to call anyone
choice_b: Call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle
choice_c: Only call your employer, not emergency services
choice_d: Use the radio only to warn other truckers
explanation: The manual advises calling for assistance before getting out of your vehicle if you have a cell phone or CB.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.20 — Crash Procedures

question: When caring for an injured person at a crash scene, when does the manual say it is acceptable to move a severely injured person?
choice_a: Whenever bystanders suggest it
choice_b: Immediately, to make them more comfortable
choice_c: Only if the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_d: Only after police give explicit permission
explanation: The manual states not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.20 — Crash Procedures

question: What two simple first-aid steps does the manual recommend for an injured person at a crash scene?
choice_a: Elevate their feet and give them water
choice_b: Loosen their clothing and call their family
choice_c: Apply a tourniquet and administer aspirin
choice_d: Stop heavy bleeding with direct pressure and keep the injured person warm
explanation: The manual recommends stopping heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound and keeping the injured person warm.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.20 — Crash Procedures

question: According to the manual, what tire-related conditions can cause a vehicle fire?
choice_a: Under-inflated tires and duals that touch
choice_b: Overinflated tires only
choice_c: New tires that have not been broken in
choice_d: Tires rotated too frequently
explanation: The manual lists under-inflated tires and duals that touch as tire-related causes of vehicle fires.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: As part of fire prevention, what should a driver verify about the fire extinguisher during the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: That it is the correct color
choice_b: That it is charged
choice_c: That it has never been used before
choice_d: That it is mounted on the passenger seat
explanation: The manual instructs drivers doing a pre-trip inspection to be sure the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: If your vehicle catches fire, what does the manual specifically warn you NOT to do?
choice_a: Notify emergency services
choice_b: Turn off the engine
choice_c: Pull into a service station
choice_d: Park in an open area away from buildings
explanation: The manual explicitly warns, 'Don't pull into a service station!' when dealing with a vehicle fire.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: Why does the manual advise keeping the doors shut on a van or box trailer that has a cargo fire?
choice_a: It keeps the cargo dry
choice_b: It prevents theft of the cargo
choice_c: It is required by shipping regulations
choice_d: Opening the doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn much faster
explanation: The manual warns that opening van doors on a cargo fire will supply the fire with oxygen, causing it to burn very fast.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: Why does the manual warn against using water on a gasoline fire?
choice_a: It will spread the flames
choice_b: It will cause an electrical shock
choice_c: It evaporates too quickly to be effective
choice_d: It reacts with gasoline to create toxic gas
explanation: The manual states you should not use water on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: What does the manual say is required to extinguish a burning tire?
choice_a: A small amount of dry chemical only
choice_b: A burning tire must be cooled, and lots of water may be required
choice_c: Sand poured directly on the flames
choice_d: A carbon dioxide extinguisher only
explanation: The manual states that a burning tire must be cooled and lots of water may be required.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.21 — Fires

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing that will sober up a person who has been drinking?
choice_a: Black coffee
choice_b: A cold shower
choice_c: Time, since the liver can process only a fixed rate of alcohol per hour
choice_d: Physical exercise
explanation: The manual explains the liver can only process about one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, a fixed rate, so only time — not coffee or a cold shower — will sober you up.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Which set of drinks does the manual say contain the same amount of alcohol?
choice_a: A 16-ounce beer, a 3-ounce glass of wine, and a 2-ounce shot of liquor
choice_b: A 12-ounce glass of wine and a 5-ounce beer
choice_c: Two 12-ounce beers and one shot of liquor
choice_d: A 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor
explanation: The manual states a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: What three factors does the manual say determine a person's Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: The amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight
choice_b: The type of alcohol, the room temperature, and the time of day
choice_c: The drinker's age, gender, and heart rate
choice_d: The food eaten, the drinker's mood, and altitude
explanation: The manual states BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Why is it dangerous that alcohol affects the part of the brain controlling judgment and self-control first?
choice_a: It causes immediate physical collapse
choice_b: It can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk
choice_c: It makes drinkers more talkative than usual
choice_d: It slows the heart rate dangerously
explanation: The manual notes that because judgment and self-control are affected first, this can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: What does a BAC of .10 mean, according to the manual?
choice_a: 10% of the blood is pure alcohol
choice_b: The driver has consumed exactly 10 standard drinks
choice_c: 1/10 of 1% (or 1/1000) of the total blood content is alcohol
choice_d: The driver's reaction time has doubled
explanation: The manual explains that a BAC of .10 means that 1/10 of 1% (or 1/1000) of your total blood content is alcohol.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Which of the following is listed by the manual as a driving error caused by alcohol?
choice_a: Signaling too early before turns
choice_b: Driving exactly at the speed limit
choice_c: Overusing turn signals
choice_d: Weaving and running over the curb
explanation: The manual lists weaving and running over the curb among the serious driving errors caused by alcohol.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Under the rules described in the manual, when is a driver permitted to possess and use a drug prescribed by a doctor?
choice_a: When the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_b: Only if the drug is taken off-duty
choice_c: Never, all prescription drugs are prohibited while driving
choice_d: Only if the employer approves it in writing
explanation: The manual states possession and use of a drug given by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: Why does the manual warn against using a drug that hides fatigue?
choice_a: Such drugs are always illegal
choice_b: The only real cure for fatigue is rest, so hiding it does not make a driver actually alert
choice_c: These drugs are more expensive than caffeine
choice_d: They interfere with the vehicle's ABS system
explanation: The manual states not to use any drug that hides fatigue, since the only cure for fatigue is rest.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.22 — Alcohol, Other Drugs, and Driving

question: How many hours of sleep does the manual say the average person needs every 24 hours?
choice_a: Four to five hours
choice_b: Five to six hours
choice_c: Seven or eight hours
choice_d: Ten to twelve hours
explanation: The manual states the average person needs seven or eight hours of sleep every 24 hours.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: According to the manual, how can a 'sleep debt' be paid off?
choice_a: By drinking coffee
choice_b: By taking vitamins
choice_c: By sheer willpower
choice_d: Only by sleeping
explanation: The manual states sleep debt can only be paid off by sleeping, and cannot be overcome by willpower.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: The manual states that many heavy motor vehicle accidents occur during which hours?
choice_a: Between midnight and 6 a.m.
choice_b: Between 6 a.m. and noon
choice_c: Between noon and 6 p.m.
choice_d: Between 6 p.m. and midnight
explanation: The manual notes many heavy motor vehicle accidents occur between midnight and 6 a.m., when tired drivers can easily fall asleep.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: How far can a commercial vehicle travel during a 4-5 second 'micro sleep' at 55 miles per hour, according to the manual?
choice_a: About 10 yards
choice_b: More than 100 yards
choice_c: About 25 feet
choice_d: Less than 20 yards
explanation: The manual states micro sleeps last around four or five seconds, and at 55 miles an hour, that's more than 100 yards — plenty of time for a crash.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: What does the manual say about the value of a short nap when a driver becomes sleepy?
choice_a: Naps are less effective than coffee
choice_b: Naps should never be shorter than two hours to be useful
choice_c: A nap as short as a half-hour will do more to overcome fatigue than a half-hour coffee stop
choice_d: Naps should only be taken at truck stops with showers
explanation: The manual states a nap as short as a half-hour will do more to overcome fatigue than a half-hour coffee stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: Which of the following is listed by the manual as a danger signal of drowsy driving?
choice_a: Frequent use of turn signals
choice_b: Increased following distance
choice_c: Checking mirrors more often than usual
choice_d: Not remembering driving the last few miles
explanation: The manual lists not remembering driving the last few miles as one of the danger signals of drowsy driving.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: What does the manual say a driver should do if they become too ill to operate a vehicle safely?
choice_a: Not drive, except in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop
choice_b: Continue driving but reduce speed
choice_c: Pull over and wait exactly one hour before continuing
choice_d: Call a relief driver only if one is available within the hour
explanation: The manual states if you become too ill to drive safely you must not drive, but in an emergency may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: What does the manual say about relying on coffee, the radio, or an open window to stay awake while driving?
choice_a: These are effective and recommended methods
choice_b: Do not rely on coffee or another source of caffeine, or count on the radio or an open window, to keep you awake
choice_c: They work only during daytime driving
choice_d: They are effective only when combined with a short nap
explanation: The manual explicitly says do not rely on coffee or caffeine, or count on the radio, an open window, or other tricks to keep you awake.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.23 — Staying Alert and Fit to Drive

question: How does the manual define 'hazardous materials'?
choice_a: Any cargo weighing over 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Only materials regulated by international law
choice_c: Products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation
choice_d: Any liquid cargo carried in a tank
explanation: The manual defines hazardous materials as products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.24 — Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers

question: Where does the manual say hazardous materials shipping papers must be kept while driving?
choice_a: In the glove compartment at all times
choice_b: Locked in the sleeper berth
choice_c: With the cargo in the trailer
choice_d: In a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within reach while driving
explanation: The manual requires shipping papers be kept in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.24 — Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers

question: According to the manual, when is a tank endorsement required?
choice_a: When your Class A or B CDL vehicle has a permanently mounted cargo tank of any capacity, or is carrying a portable tank of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_b: Whenever hazardous materials of any kind are being hauled
choice_c: Only when transporting flammable gases specifically
choice_d: Only for vehicles requiring a Class C CDL
explanation: The manual states a tank endorsement is required if your Class A or B CDL vehicle has a permanently mounted cargo tank of any capacity or carries a portable tank of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.24 — Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers

question: What size must a hazardous materials placard be, according to the manual?
choice_a: At least 8 inches square
choice_b: At least 10 3/4 inches square
choice_c: At least 12 inches square
choice_d: At least 6 inches square
explanation: The manual states placards must be at least 10 3/4 inches square, turned upright on a point in a diamond shape.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.24 — Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers

question: What letters precede the four-digit identification number used to identify hazardous materials, per the manual?
choice_a: The letters "HM"
choice_b: The letters "DOT"
choice_c: The letters "NA" or "UN"
choice_d: The letters "EPA"
explanation: The manual states the identification number will be preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN," and the US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook lists chemicals and their identification numbers.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.24 — Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers
